title: Feltsense AI Engineer
description: About the company We raised $5.1M to build agents that operate as fully autonomous founders. Our backers include Matt Schlicht (founder of Moltbook), the founders of Crunchbase and Republic, and VCs including Draper, Precursor, and Liquid2. We're working at the frontier of autonomous systems, building agents that don't just chat, but run entire businesses. Our system identifies business opportunities through market signals, validates ideas with live ad tests, builds and launches software products, and brings in human experts wherever agents fall short. That loop already runs end to end: from idea to launched product to first revenue. Over the next 12 months, our focus is on reliability, throughput, and self-improvement, making every launch better than the last. About the role We're looking for a hands-on AI Engineer to take ownership of the architecture and development of our autonomous agent system. You'll lead the technical direction of the platform, building multi-agent orchestration systems, self-improving agent harnesses, and AI-powered backend services. This is a highly technical leadership role that combines architectural decision-making with hands-on engineering. You'll be expected to ship production code, make key technical decisions, improve agent behavior in production, and help establish the engineering standards as the company scales. Responsibilities Own the system architecture and make key technical decisions across the platform. Design and build multi-agent systems and orchestration infrastructure that take products from idea to launch. Develop self-improving agent harnesses, including feedback loops, evaluation systems, and memory. Build and maintain AI-powered backend services on top of LLM APIs such as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini. Write production code, particularly around agent runtime and orchestration. Debug and improve AI behavior in production through prompt engineering, structured outputs, retries, and fallbacks. Break down complex technical challenges into actionable milestones and prioritize the engineering roadmap. Establish engineering standards around code reviews, testing, observability, and release processes. Lead and support the engineering team while remaining deeply involved in implementation. Requirements 4+ years of professional software engineering experience. Previous technical leadership experience at an early-stage company (Founding Engineer, Tech Lead, Head of Engineering, or similar). Hands-on experience building and shipping multi-agent systems and orchestration frameworks to production. Experience developing self-improving or self-evolving agent harnesses. Strong backend engineering skills, including designing and maintaining APIs, services, and data flows. Experience working with LLM-based systems, including prompt engineering, model configuration, structured outputs, embeddings, retrieval, and evaluation. Daily hands-on experience with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, or similar tools. You should know how to delegate work to agents, review their output, and verify what they build. Nice to have Strong TypeScript and Node.js experience. Experience with Vercel AI SDK, Claude Agent SDK, or building custom agent runtimes. Experience with PostgreSQL, Supabase, and pgvector. Familiarity with background job systems such as Inngest or Pub/Sub. Experience with Zod, Vitest, and GCP Cloud Run. Experience growing or restructuring distributed engineering teams. title: Head of AI Native Operations
description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We are looking for a Head of AI Native Operations to build the autonomous systems that run Supabase. Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system, where agents carry the operational load end to end. We are standing up a new central team to build that platform and run it in production. This is the role that leads it, and it is hands-on. You design the architecture, build the first versions of the critical pieces, and are accountable for whether every agent we run is correct, safe, and improving over time. We build rather than buy, and there are no settled best practices for most of this yet, so you will be setting them. You will lead a team of senior individual contributors extending the platform and driving adoption across teams. What You’ll Be Responsible For In this role, you’ll: Own the agent platform architecture: The harness and orchestration layer and connectors into company systems, shared context and memory, and the path from prototype to production. Catch regressions before they ship: Model, prompt, and tool changes can’t ship until they pass the evals. When a new model comes out, you know within hours whether to adopt it. Make every agent observable: Every run and every decision is traced. For any agent at any time, you can answer what it did, why, what it cost, and how its quality is trending. Own safety and trust: Design the controls that let agents act without a human in the loop: least-privilege credentials, hard policy limits, escalation thresholds, audit logs, sandboxing, and prompt-injection defenses. Replace workflows, don’t assist them: Pick the workflows agents can fully own today and take them to production. Turn wins into a platform: Package what works into reusable components, templates, and eval harnesses so other teams can ship their own production agents without starting from scratch. Build and direct the team: Hire and grow senior ICs, review their designs and pull requests, and hold the quality bar. Measure what matters: Track workflows automated, eval pass rates, cost per run, and work absorbed against the hiring plan. How You’ll Think A Point of View on Where Automation Wins You have a thesis about how AI and automation change the way a company operates, and it comes from building, not reading. You can look at a business and say which workflows agents can own today, which they will own in 12 months as models improve, and which still need people, and why. You defend that view with evidence from systems you have shipped, and you update it when the evals tell you to. Eval-Driven You don’t trust an agent because the demo looked good. You trust it because it passes a test set of real cases, and you know which cases it fails. When anything changes, your first question is “what do the evals say?” Inversion Thinking Left alone, an autonomous system tends to fail quietly, or people route around it. So the first question about any agent isn’t “does it work on the happy path?” but “how will this break, and how will we know?” The design follows from that answer: what the agent is never allowed to do, what it escalates, and which alert fires when quality drifts. Recursive Thinking Every system you build should produce the evidence that grades it. An agent isn’t done when it works. It’s done when it tells you, without you in the loop, that it has stopped working. Must Have Hands-on agent building: Have personally designed and built autonomous agent or LLM systems that ran in production and that others depended on. Prototypes, demos, and configuring a vendor tool don’t count. You don’t need to be a career software engineer, but you must have built these systems yourself. Architecture depth: Can explain how the pieces fit together (orchestration, tool and data access, context and memory, tracing, evals, guardrails, deployment), with opinions on current frameworks. Security judgment: Have shipped agents that take real actions with real permissions, and designed the controls that made that safe. A tested point of view: Can argue, with examples from your own builds, where autonomous systems create real business leverage and where they don’t yet. Technical leadership: Have led senior builders and set the quality bar through design and code review. Strong Signal Have replaced a human-run business workflow (finance, operations, support, release management) end to end with an autonomous system. Are native to Git, Markdown, and pull requests, and comfortable reading and writing Python or TypeScript. Have taken an internal platform from zero to adoption by teams you did not control. A software engineering background is a plus, but not required. What Success Looks Like Six months: 20+ autonomous agents in production on the shared platform, each with an eval suite, tracing, and a named owner. Regressions get caught, not discovered: Quality problems surface in an alert or dashboard before a user reports them. Workflows replaced, not assisted: Multiple high-volume workflows are fully owned by agents, with humans handling only escalations. Trusted by default: No agent causes material financial, security, or customer harm, and every agent’s permissions and actions can be audited. Teams ship their own: At least three teams outside the core team run production agents built on the platform. Autonomous team: Your two reports work independently, and you spend your time on architecture and review rather than execution. What We Offer Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. About the Team Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. ~400 team members 60+ countries 20+ languages spoken Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.
